headline: High: Pipecat can stream sensitive audio/text to broad-egress Plane workflows, creating default leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat exposes stdin/stdout and shared-bus session state, while Plane has file uploads and broad egress, so a manual or indirect content bridge is plausible. However, no shared channel or parser is documented, and Plane cannot run browsers or write its filesystem, limiting direct hijack pathways.
conditions: IF an operator copies Pipecat output into Plane notes or uploads it as a task artifact
IF Plane ingests Pipecat-generated text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste template that strips instructions
Mark Pipecat outputs as data-only before pasting
Disable automatic task creation from pasted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, and can call many third-party APIs with allowlisted egress. Plane stores issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes with broad egress. In default use, sensitive conversational content can flow into Plane artifacts or external services, so leakage is plausible even without a shared filesystem.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards conversation transcripts or media into Plane tasks or file uploads
IF Plane exports stored notes or attachments to external services
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive test data
Turn off or review any automatic transcript export
Limit Plane project visibility to the smallest team
Delete uploaded artifacts after triage
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat supports multiple instances with shared-bus session scope, while Plane supports multiple instances but has no write_filesystem capability listed. Because Plane cannot write the filesystem and no overlapping mutable resource is documented, direct write-write conflict is limited; uncertainty stays low rather than none because shared-bus coordination is still present on Pipecat.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable resource through an unlisted integration
IF an orchestrator maps Pipecat shared-bus state into Plane-side writes
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate workspaces
Avoid concurrent edits to the same ticket set
Serialize handoffs through one operator
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can generate speech/transcript content and Plane can store and route tasks, notes, and hyperlinks. If Plane treats Pipecat output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into task creation or scheduling decisions. Plane has no documented verification gate, so the pair is risky in default workflow integrations.
conditions: IF Pipecat output is copied into Plane without human verification
IF Plane automation creates tasks from Pipecat transcripts or summaries
mitigations: Require human review before task creation
Add a checklist for factual claims
Store raw Pipecat output separately from action items
Disable auto-import of transcripts
requires-engineering: add validation rules before task creation

E_compliance.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, which can include regulated content, while Plane stores files, notes, and tasks and offers broad egress. No residency, retention, or certification controls are documented for either agent, so compliance mismatch is plausible; uncertainty escalates above low because the data classes are broad and the pair can move sensitive content into Plane.
conditions: IF regulated audio or transcript data is stored in Plane
IF Plane retention or export settings differ from the source system
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Plane
Review retention settings in both systems
Limit exports to approved regions
Document the data flow for auditors
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
